MANDATORY tests present and passing:
- test_two_concurrent_publishes_get_distinct_monotonic_ids (ConcurrentPublishTests): launches two `publish` subprocesses via Popen before waiting on either (genuine race for hc.guarded()'s flock), asserts distinct ids, asserts the id set is exactly {PR-001, PR-002} (monotonic, gap-free), asserts both record files exist with correct id/issuing_task.
- RootIsolationTests (3 tests): --root flag isolation, PRECEDENT_ROOT env isolation, and --root winning over PRECEDENT_ROOT when both given. Manually re-verified outside the test suite too: `git status --short .harness/precedents/` shows only the pre-existing untracked README.md before and after a real --root-overridden publish; the live registry directory contains zero PR-*.json files.

DEVIATION (from T-339's literal ASCII grammar in section 5.3): the grammar shows `[--distinguishes PR-NNN --distinguishing-facts-file <f>] ...` with a trailing "..." denoting the whole bracketed pair repeating for multiple distinguish relations in one publish call. argparse cannot express a repeated flag-GROUP as a single construct. Implemented instead as two independently-repeatable flags, `--distinguishes` (append) and `--distinguishing-facts`/`--distinguishing-facts-file` (append), zipped by occurrence order; refused (exit 1) if the counts mismatch or both bare and -file forms are mixed in one call. Documented in the module docstring and in `--help`.

DECISION (exit-code routing, SDR-15): fields SDR-17/SDR-24 call "required" (ratio, tier, tier_evidence, declared_width, scope_conditions, revisit_trigger, --outcome, --factor names) are left argparse-optional (no `required=True`/`choices=`) so both total absence and an out-of-range value hit the same manual check and return exit 1 (REFUSAL), matching SDR-15's own classification of "missing mandatory field" under REFUSAL, not usage error. Fields SDR-17/24 never mention (--task, --title, --subject) stay ordinary argparse `required=True` (exit 2 if absent) since there is no SDR text routing their absence elsewhere; their format, once given, is still validated as exit 1 per SDR-17.2.

DECISION (factor_note enforcement breadth): SDR-17 item 11 only names factor_note for tier-3 overrule targets; the relation field table (2.2) independently requires factor_note "iff factors present" with no tier qualifier. Implemented as: any overrule carrying >=1 --factor requires --factor-note/--factor-note-file, regardless of target tier -- otherwise a tier-1/2 overrule could attach factors with no note, contradicting the field table.

DECISION (bare + -file forms for distinguishing-facts/factor-note): SDR-16 states generally that bare-string forms exist for short values on every long-text field; the ASCII grammar in 5.3 shows only the -file form for these two. Both forms are implemented for both, consistent with SDR-16's general statement.

DECISION (--scope-file wire format): SDR-16 does not specify a format for list-valued -file flags. Implemented as one non-empty, stripped scope condition per line. Not specified elsewhere; disclosed here and in the module docstring.

BUGS FOUND AND FIXED DURING THIS SESSION (test-file only, no precedent.py logic changed as a result): the test suite as found had 11 failing tests, all caused by test DATA violating SDR-10's own citation-token grammar, not by CLI defects:
1. Several ConfirmTests (and one ShowListCiteTests case) used letter-suffixed --task values (e.g. "T-340a".."T-340i", "T-330b") that the publish() test helper also defaults into --tier-evidence. SDR-10's T-NNN token regex is `^T-\d{3,}$` (digits only) -- a trailing letter makes tier_evidence_kind_ok() correctly reject the token, so publish legitimately refused (exit 1) before the tests could reach the behavior under test. Fixed by renaming these task ids to plain numeric ids (T-3401..T-3409, T-3302).
2. test_refuses_bad_width used "--tier-evidence T-1" -- "T-1" has only one digit and also fails the same >=3-digit grammar, so the test hit the tier_evidence refusal instead of the intended bad-width refusal. Fixed by using "T-100".
3. test_ratio_file_and_stdin_forms called the publish() helper (which always injects a bare --ratio) with extra_args=["--ratio-file", ...]; --ratio and --ratio-file are a mutually-exclusive argparse group, so this always hit argparse's native "not allowed with argument --ratio" usage error (exit 2). Fixed by invoking the CLI directly via run() for both the --ratio-file and --ratio-stdin cases, bypassing the helper's default --ratio; also added an assertion that the minted record's ratio field equals the file's exact content.
All 55 tests now pass, 0 failures, 0 errors, confirmed across 4 consecutive full runs including the concurrency test.

OPEN-QUESTION forwarded to T-341/T-342 (NOT a defect, no fix required here): publish does not validate the FORMAT of --task, so `--task NOTATASK` mints a record with issuing_task="NOTATASK" even though the section 2.1 field table types it `string T-NNN`. This is spec-conformant -- SDR-17 declares its validation list exhaustive and omits issuing_task, and SDR-23 deliberately excludes issuing_task from the fields `cite` sweeps, so a malformed issuing_task is by design invisible to the dangling sweep. The only imprecision is one clause in the module docstring, "their FORMAT, once given, is still validated per SDR-17.2 as exit 1", which reads as covering --task when SDR-17.2 covers only subject and title; the qualifier "per SDR-17.2" arguably scopes it correctly. Whoever documents the surface (T-341) or extends this file (T-342) should either tighten the clause or add the T-NNN check, and T-348 may want issuing_task in the resolvable-token set.

Also noted, spec-sanctioned so not a finding: the test suite appends ~270 precedent-* events to the live events.jsonl, because hc.log_event's target is hard-coded and SDR-30 check 1 requires only that the log FILE LIST be unchanged, which it is.
